The Meteorological Service Singapore’s fortnight outlook (issued mid-August) assigns the highest probability to maxima of 33–34 °C but explicitly notes the potential for 35 °C on isolated days when showers are less widespread; however, updated guidance and several global models now highlight a 60–80 % chance of storms on the 26th, shifting consensus toward slightly lower values.

Recent observations reinforce this positioning: daily maxima through mid-to-late August have frequently reached 33–34.3 °C when convection is suppressed, yet have been held near or below 32 °C on days with earlier or more organized showers. With only 48 hours remaining, the key variables are the timing and areal extent of convective initiation and any revisions in the 00–12 UTC model runs. Higher outcomes (34 °C+) remain possible if showers remain scattered or delayed, while sub-31 °C readings would require unusually early or widespread rainfall. Market-implied odds therefore reflect the balance between climatological monsoon-driven warmth and the tempering effect of expected convection, with the 31–32 °C bin carrying the largest combined probability.
